title: Realtime prefix stitching and fragment reconciliation for prompt-cache deduplication
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Introduce a realtime "stitching" layer for prefix cache entries that identifies and merges overlapping prefix fragments across concurrent requests and across KV shards, with a reconciliation pass to ensure deterministic KV lookup results. Goal is to reduce redundant KV storage on GPU memory and improve cache hit quality for continuous batching workloads.
problem_statement: We observe a high rate of near-duplicate prefix fragments stored in the GPU-resident KV cache when many similar prompts are served concurrently (templated prompts, minor slot differences). This increases GPU memory pressure, reduces effective batch density, and increases OOM risk on large-context models. Current heuristics dedupe at coarse granularity and miss overlapping substrings and shifted-token prefixes.
proposed_solution: 1) At insertion time, compute a short-content fingerprint (rolling hash + token-length signature) and a content-anchor summary for each fragment. 2) Maintain a lightweight in-GPU bloom+fingerprint index to detect candidate overlaps. 3) For candidates, attempt a stitched fragment write: allocate a new compact slab that references the non-overlapping tails and points into existing fragments for shared spans using offset references. 4) Reconciliation pass: a background ephemeral worker reconciles references to concrete KV slices, collapses unnecessary indirections, and updates reference counts atomically with an epoch number to preserve replay determinism. 5) Provide a fallback path that copies full fragments when stitching fails or would increase lookup latency.
technical_notes: - Fingerprinting: 64-bit rolling Rabin hash on token ids + 16-bit token-length bucket. - Index: GPU-resident cuckoo-bloom hybrid for candidate lookups (approx 1-2% false positive). - Slab layout: short runs inline, mid runs as (base_fragment_id, offset, length). - Epochs: every write gets epoch id; readers pin epoch to get a stable view. - Reconciliation: single-threaded per-shard worker to avoid global contention; uses compare-and-swap to update root pointers. - Metric instrumentation: per-write latency, stitch_probe_count, successful_stitches, stitching_latency_p50/p95, memory_delta_bytes. - Safety: ensure no KV pointer is dereferenced after free; use refcount+epoch barrier. - API: new config flags on runtime: kv.stitching.enabled, kv.stitch.quality_threshold, kv.stitch.inline_max_tokens.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for fingerprint collision handling and false-positive mitigation
Integration test that stitches overlapping prefixes and preserves decode outputs for existing prompts (deterministic replay)
Benchmark: GPU KV memory used by median template-heavy 8k-conversation workload reduced by >= 18%
P95 token generation latency regression <= 2ms compared to baseline for common batch sizes
No increase in incorrect generations caused by stale KV reads in 1000-run smoke harness
Feature gated behind kv.stitching.enabled and rollout flag; telemetry logged for every stitch decision
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime config and remote feature-flagging (canary -> gradual)
Phase 1: Deploy read-only probe mode in dev for 2 weeks (collect stitch candidate metrics only)
Phase 2: Enable stitching on 5% of requests in staging and run decode-integrity tests overnight
Phase 3: Canary in production on non-critical clusters (10% traffic) for 72h, monitor errors and perf
Phase 4: Gradual ramp to 100% with automatic rollback if error rate or latency regressions exceed thresholds
test_plan: Unit: fingerprint generation, index false positive windows, refcount increments/decrements
Integration: end-to-end generation reproductions against golden-output corpus (templated prompts with slot variation)
Load: 2x peak QPS simulation with continuous-batching profile to measure memory delta and batch density
Chaos: force shard worker restart during reconciliation to verify recovery and correctness
Security: memory-safety fuzzing of slab stitching path
progress_updates: 2025-02-16: Spike completed. Prototype shows ~22% memory reduction on synthetic templated workload but with a 4ms median stitch hit penalty.
2025-02-21: Microbenchmarks: optimized bloom index reduced probe cost by 40%; stitching median latency now ~1.1ms.
2025-02-25: Design review with infra and runtime teams. Agreed to use epoch-based reads to avoid global locks. Action: write CAS-based pointer update RFC.
2025-03-01: RFC posted: link in linked_docs. Experiment harness prepared; staging job scheduled for Phase 1 on 2025-03-05.
2025-03-03: Implemented basic reconciliation worker; initial integration tests passing locally. Observed occasional refcount leak under forced reconnect; debugging in progress.
blockers: Need final sign-off from memory-safety review (security) before enabling in production
Edge-case: reconciling fragments across shards when a fragment migrates due to re-sharding; requires cross-shard coordination protocol (design pending)
